sources.title: Dikran D. Dikranjan, Introduction to Topological Groups (author lecture notes, Udine/Madrid 2007, 69 pp.)
sources.locator: Introduction and §§1.1-1.2, printed pp. 1-13; §§3.1-3.2, printed pp. 5-8; §§7.1-7.3, printed pp. 46-52. The complete text was downloaded and inspected; the dual-group sections 7.1-7.3 were read in full.

contents.name: Introduction: T = R/Z is a compact divisible abelian group topologically isomorphic to the unitary circle S
Section 1.1, Lemmas 1.17-1.19 and Example 1.20: quotient maps of topological groups are open and R/Z is isomorphic to T as a topological group
Exercise 3.20 (printed pp. 9–10), Theorem 4.37 and Corollary 4.40 (printed pp. 29–31): closed subgroups of R and Rn and the structure of Rn/H
contents.reason: The actual Dikranjan closed-subgroup and quotient classification is not needed by the selected real-character covering/Cauchy proof or the finite-coordinate Euclidean-dual computation.

contents.name: Section 3.1, Definition of a topological group, and §3.2.2, topologies generated by characters
Section 7.1, Definition of G* and the compact-open neighbourhoods W(K,U) of the dual group
Section 7.1, Example 7.1(1): a compact abelian group has discrete dual
Section 7.1, Example 7.1(2): a discrete abelian group has compact dual
Section 7.1, Theorem 7.2(a)-(b): the arc criterion x in Lambda_k iff x,2x,...,kx in Lambda_1 and the continuity test chi^{-1}(Lambda_1)
Section 7.1, Theorem 7.2(c)-(e): compact-open neighbourhood base, addition estimates, and closedness of W(K,F)
Section 7.1, Theorem 7.2(f): a relatively compact neighbourhood has compact closure, so the dual of an LCA group is locally compact
Section 7.1, Corollary 7.3: the inclusion of the dual into the compact group of all homomorphisms is an embedding iff the group is discrete
contents.reason: This criterion compares the dual with all possibly discontinuous homomorphisms; no scaffolded FR-15 item or later consumer uses it, and it contributes nothing to local compactness or to the four examples.

contents.name: Section 7.2, Proposition 7.4: continuous open surjective homomorphisms factor through their kernels
Section 7.2, Lemma 7.5: every continuous endomorphism of T is k times the identity, k in Z
Section 7.2, Example 7.7: the dual of T is Z
Section 7.2, Example 7.7: the dual of Z is T
Section 7.2, Example 7.7: the dual of R is R
Section 7.2, Example 7.7 and Exercises 7.8-7.10: duals of Z(p-infinity), Jp and Qp
contents.reason: p-adic and Prufer-group duals are outside the commissioned FR-15 scope, and no scaffolded item, B-page example or registered consumer of this pair uses them.

contents.name: Section 7.3, Lemma 7.12: the dual of a finite direct product is the product of the duals, homeomorphically
Section 7.3, Theorem 7.14: the dual of a discrete direct sum is the product of the duals; the dual of a product of compact groups is the direct sum of the duals
Section 7.3, Proposition 7.13: Hom(Z_n, T) is isomorphic to Z_n for the finite cyclic group of order n
Section 7.3, Exercise 7.11: characters of subgroups of Rn extend to Rn
contents.reason: Character extension from closed subgroups is proved there from biduality and annihilator exactness; the FR-15 foundation is deliberately biduality-free and needs no extension theorem.

contents.name: Sections 5-6, Folner's theorem, Peter-Weyl, and separation of points by characters
contents.reason: Point separation and compact-group orthogonality are developed inversion-first on the duality pair and must not be imported into this foundation, whose design removes the circular compact-group route.

contents.name: Sections 7.4-8, natural transformation, duality theorem 7.36, structure and exactness
contents.reason: Biduality, exactness and the natural transformation are exactly the subject of that planned pair; the present foundation stops before inversion and biduality by design.

sources.title: Lynn H. Loomis, Introduction to Abstract Harmonic Analysis, D. Van Nostrand 1953, Chapter VII
sources.locator: Chapter VII, §§34-35, printed pp. 134-140. The scanned full text was downloaded and the OCR text of 34A-34E and 35A-35E was read.

contents.name: 34A: characters are the continuous homomorphisms into the complex numbers of modulus one, and (x, M) -> a_M(x) is jointly continuous
34A/definition: every character of G is a continuous homomorphism into the multiplicative unit circle
34B: every character arises from a regular maximal ideal of L1(G), identifying the dual with the maximal-ideal space
contents.reason: The L1/Gelfand identification of the character space is FR-16 material; this foundation defines the dual directly as continuous homomorphisms and deliberately avoids the group-algebra route.

contents.name: 34C: the topology of the dual is uniform convergence on compact sets, with basis U(C, eps, a0)
34D: the pointwise product of characters is a character, and the dual is a locally compact abelian group
34E: remark on the sign convention relating the character a_M to the Fourier transform
contents.reason: A convention remark about the transform normalisation; the library fixes its LCA transform convention on the FR-6 and FR-16 pages, and no FR-15 claim depends on this remark.

contents.name: 35A: the character group of a direct product is the product of the character groups, with the product topology
35B: the character group of G/H is the annihilator of H, with its topology from compact lifts
35C: every character of R is e^{iyx}, and R-hat is isomorphic and homeomorphic to R
35D: the characters of R/I are e^{2 pinx}, and the dual of R/I is the integers I
35E: the characters of the integers I are e^{2 pixn} with 0 <= x < 1, and the dual of I is R/I

sources.title: Manfred Einsiedler and Thomas Ward, Ergodic Theory with a View Towards Number Theory, Appendix C (course-hosted full text)
sources.locator: Appendix C, §§C.1-C.3, printed pp. 429-439. The full PDF was downloaded and Appendix C.1 and C.3 were read.

contents.name: C.1: translations and inversion are homeomorphisms and the closure of a subgroup is a subgroup
C.1: G/H carries the quotient topology, the quotient map is open, and G/H is a topological group for closed normal H
C.3: definition of a character chi: G -> S1 and the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets via N(K, eps)
C.3, Theorem C.6: the character group of an LCA group is itself an LCA group
C.3, Theorem C.6: a subgroup of the dual separating points is dense
contents.reason: Density of separating subgroups is used together with inversion and biduality on the planned duality pair and is not needed for the closure, local-compactness or example claims of FR-15.

contents.name: C.3, Lemma C.7: discrete groups have compact duals and compact groups have discrete duals, with the L1 orthogonality proof
C.3, Theorem C.13: H-perp is closed and the dual of G/H is H-perp
C.3, Theorem C.13: the remaining annihilator exactness identities (G-hat/H-perp, H1-perp + H2-perp, H-perp-perp)
contents.reason: These identities are proved there from biduality and belong to the exactness development of the planned duality pair.

contents.name: C.3, Example C.14(1): the map z -> chi_z with chi_z(1) = z is an isomorphism S1 -> Z-hat
C.3, Example C.14(2): every character of R is t -> e^{ist}, so R-hat is isomorphic to R
C.3, after Lemma C.7: for T = R/Z the dual is {chi_k} with chi_k(t) = e^{2 pikt}
C.3, Example C.14(3)-(4): duals of locally compact fields and of Qp
contents.reason: Local-field and p-adic duals are not commissioned for this pair, and neither the A page nor the four B examples consume them.

contents.name: C.3, Theorem C.11: characters of a compact abelian group separate points and form an orthonormal basis of L2
contents.reason: Compact-group character completeness is obtained there from inversion and Plancherel; importing it here would reintroduce the circular compact-group route the design removes.

contents.name: C.3, Theorem C.10 (printed p. 436): Fourier inversion on L1(G) intersect B(G)
contents.reason: The actual EW inversion theorem concerns a Haar Fourier transform and the positive-definite class B(G); FR15 constructs the dual topologically without an inversion assertion. FR16 is the approved inversion destination.

contents.name: C.3, Theorem C.12 (printed p. 437): the evaluation map G to its bidual is an LCA isomorphism
contents.reason: The actual EW biduality theorem asserts evaluation-map surjectivity for every LCA group. FR15 supplies joint evaluation and elementary duals but no general double-dual identification; FR17 is the approved biduality destination.

contents.name: C.2, Theorem C.4: existence and uniqueness of Haar measure on locally compact groups
C.3, Lemma C.15: Riemann-Lebesgue for measures absolutely continuous with respect to Haar measure
contents.reason: The LCA Riemann-Lebesgue lemma is a consequence of joint evaluation proved on the planned Bochner/inversion pair, not an FR-15 claim.

contents.name: Section 7.2, Lemma 7.5 and Example 7.7: the continuous endomorphisms of T are k times the identity, so T-hat is Z
Section 7.2, Example 7.7: the dual of Z is T via chi -> chi(1)
Section 7.2, Example 7.7: the dual of R is R via the characters chi_r(x) = chi_1(rx)
Section 7.3, Proposition 7.13 and Theorem 7.14: Hom(Z_n, T) is isomorphic to Z_n and the dual of a finite discrete direct sum is the product of the duals
Section 7.3, Theorem 7.14 second part: the dual of a product of compact groups is the direct sum of the duals
contents.reason: Compact-product duality is not needed for the four concrete examples and is subsumed by the later biduality and exactness development of the planned duality pair.

contents.name: C.3, Example C.14(1): S1 -> Z-hat is an isomorphism
C.3, Example C.14(2): R-hat is isomorphic to R
C.3: for T = R/Z the characters are chi_k(t) = e^{2 pikt}, k in Z
C.3, Theorem C.12 and C.13: biduality and annihilator exactness
contents.reason: These are the planned duality pair's own results; the examples on this page use only the concrete dual computations listed above.
